abstract.para: &hawk; (&haweb;) is a graphical Web interface for configuring, monitoring and managing &sleha; clusters. &hawk;'s user-friendly Web interface allows you to monitor and administer your High Availability clusters from Linux or non-Linux machines alike. &hawk; can be accessed from any machine inside or outside of the cluster by using a (graphical) Web browser.

section.title: Requirements
section.para: Before users can log in to &hawk;, the following requirements need to be fulfilled:

listitem.para: The hawk2 package must be installed on all cluster nodes you want to connect to with &hawk;.
On the machine from which to access a cluster node using &hawk;, you need a (graphical) Web browser (with JavaScript and cookies enabled) to establish the connection.
To use &hawk;, the respective Web service must be started on the node that you want to connect to via the Web interface.
If you have set up your cluster with the bootstrap scripts provided by the &crmshell;, the &hawk; service is already enabled.

varlistentry.term: Username, group, and password on each cluster node

listitem.para: &hawk; users must be members of the haclient group. The installation creates a Linux user named hacluster, who is added to the haclient group.

When using the crm cluster init script for setup, a default password is set for the hacluster user. Before starting &hawk;, change it to a secure password. If you did not use the crm cluster init script, either set a password for the hacluster first or create a new user which is a member of the haclient group. Do this on every node you will connect to with &hawk;.

A wild card certificate is a public key certificate that is valid for multiple sub-domains. For example, a wild card certificate for *.&exampledomain; secures the domains www.&exampledomain;, login.&exampledomain;, and more.
&hawk; supports wild card certificates as well as conventional certificates. A self-signed default private key and certificate is generated by /srv/www/hawk/bin/generate-ssl-cert.
To use your own certificate (conventional or wild card), replace the generated certificate at /etc/ssl/certs/hawk.pem with your own.

section.para: By default, users logged in as &rootuser; or hacluster have full read-write access to all cluster configuration tasks. However, Access Control Lists (ACLs) can be used to define fine-grained access permissions.

If ACLs are enabled in the CRM, the available functions in &hawk; depend on the user role and their assigned access permissions. The History Explorer in &hawk; can only be executed by the user hacluster.

section.title: Top-level row
section.para: &hawk;'s top-level row shows the following entries:

listitem.para: Batch: Click to switch to batch mode. This allows you to simulate and stage changes and to apply them as a single transaction.
USERNAME: Allows you to set preferences for &hawk; (for example, the language for the Web interface, or whether to display a warning if &stonith; is disabled).
Help: Access the &productname; documentation, read the release notes or report a bug.
Logout: Click to log out.

section.title: Left navigation bar
section.para: After logging in to &hawk;, you will see a navigation bar on the left-hand side and a top-level row with several links on the right-hand side.

listitem.para: Status: Displays the current cluster status at a glance. If your cluster includes guest nodes (nodes that run the pacemaker_remote daemon), they are displayed, too. The screen refreshes in near real-time: any status changes for nodes or resources are visible almost immediately.

Dashboard: Allows you to monitor multiple clusters. If your cluster includes guest nodes (nodes that run the pacemaker_remote daemon), they are displayed, too. The screen refreshes in near real-time: any status changes for nodes or resources are visible almost immediately.
History: Opens the History Explorer from which you can generate cluster reports.
Command Log: Lists the &crmsh; commands recently executed by &hawk;.
Add Resource: Opens the resource configuration screen.
Add Constraint: Opens the constraint configuration screen.
Wizards: Allows you to select from several wizards that guide you through the creation of resources for a certain workload, for example, a DRBD block device.
Edit Configuration: Allows you to edit resources, constraints, node names and attributes, tags, alerts, and fencing topologies.
Cluster Configuration: Allows you to modify global cluster options and resource and operation defaults.
Access Control Roles : Opens a screen where you can create roles for access control lists (sets of rules describing access rights to the CIB).
Access Control Targets : Opens a screen where you can create targets (system users) for access control lists and assign roles to them.
